title: Best Corporate Video Producers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a corporate video producer for company, recruitment or training videos: what to include, how to brief it, price factors and red flags.
intro: Corporate videos present a company to customers, investors, job candidates or employees: brand films, recruitment videos, announcements, testimonials and event recaps. Online producers often edit footage you film, create animated corporate videos or combine interviews with graphics. Projects go wrong when the message is vague, approvals involve too many people, or people appear without consent. This guide helps you plan a clear corporate video.

faq.q: What types of corporate videos are common?
faq.a: Company introductions, recruitment videos, customer testimonials, internal announcements, training, event highlights and investor updates.

faq.q: Do I need to film anything?
faq.a: For live-action videos, usually yes, unless you hire a local crew. Many online producers edit your footage or create animated videos.
Decide early. Too many reviewers slow projects and lead to conflicting feedback. Name one decision maker.

faq.q: Do people in the video need to give permission?
faq.a: Yes. Get written consent from employees, customers and anyone else who appears, especially for public use.

faq.q: How long should a corporate video be?
faq.a: Usually short: long enough for one clear message. Longer versions can live on your website for those who want more.
